themes.title: General – Textile Fibers & Synthetic Yarn Manufacturing

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Raj Rayon Industries as an SVG Group-revived, vertically integrated polyester yarn manufacturer at Silvassa - "from insolvency-led default to investment-grade stability" - now at an inflection point with a Rs 650 crore brownfield Phase II expansion towards ~700 ++ TPD and a mix shift into value-added, specialty and recycled products.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established 1993 at Silvassa; production halted in 2018 amid financial distress and the company was acquired by SVG Group in 2021 through insolvency proceedings under the NCLT, with commercial production revived in January 2023.
- SVG ecosystem: SVG Fashions (established 1984) is described as "India's leading vertically integrated producer of polyester knits", with 40+ years of textile expertise; RRIL's upstream operations support SVG's downstream business, giving captive demand and supply-chain security during ramp-up, and end-brand clients include Adidas, Reebok, Asics, Cult, Skechers, Jockey, Reliance Retail, D Mart, V Mart and V2 Retail.
- Quality premium and approval base: RRIL "commands a 1-2% pricing premium over many industry peers" on consistent product quality, lot continuity and established brand trust, with 3,500+ customer approvals built in three operating years across India and 15+ export markets - the deck argues qualification work is already complete for the expanded capacity.
- Continuous melt integration converts PET directly into fibre, eliminating the chip cost layer; the deck states there are "Only 14 direct melt manufacturers in India - the remaining 26-30 chip-buyers carry a structural cost disadvantage".
- Credit rating journey runs from IND D / IND D (Issuer Not Cooperating) during the SDR and plant-shutdown years to "IND BBB+ / Stable (Affirmed)", citing linkages with a strong parent, successful turnaround of operations and adequate liquidity.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- SVG's 2021 takeover funding: Equity (Share Capital) Rs 54.9 Cr + CCPS (2.5 Mn @ Rs 100) Rs 25.0 Cr + Unsecured Loan from SVG Rs 45.0 Cr = Total SVG Capital Infused Rs 124.9 Cr; the CCPS converts to equity at face value by 2029.
- Legacy creditor settlement of Rs 80 Cr (Rs 55 Cr cash + Rs 25 Cr CCPS) via NCLT resolution, with "No contingent liabilities remain post-CIRP".
- Debt structure post-acquisition: Total Term Loans (BoB + HDFC) Rs 268.5 Cr sanctioned - Bank of Baroda Rs 185 Cr (repaid Rs 66.69 Cr, outstanding Rs 118.31 Cr) and HDFC Bank Rs 83.5 Cr (drawn Rs 64.73 Cr, balance to be drawn by Q2-Q3FY27, repaid Rs 3.5 Cr); combined working capital limit enhanced from Rs 60 Cr initial to Rs 270 Cr current, with utilisation predominantly non-fund-based.
- FY27 deleveraging target of ~Rs 60 Cr "via surplus cash & targeted prepayment".
- Structurally negative working capital cycle: raw materials are sourced on supplier credit backed by non-fund-based facilities and the entire production-to-collection cycle is completed within the supplier credit period, a self-funded position the deck expects to be sustained going forward.
- Tax shield is stated two different ways in the same deck: "Rs 450 Cr of unabsorbed tax losses carried forward" (transaction-structure slide) and "approximately Rs 400 Crores of unabsorbed tax losses and depreciation" (structural-advantages slide). Both are reported as printed.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulation] BIS certification is now mandatory for all imported POY and FDY yarns in India, restricting cheap Chinese imports, and a Minimum Import Price (MIP) on fabrics "creates an additional layer of protection for domestic manufacturers".
- [Trade access] India-EU FTA (January 2026) and US-India Trade Framework (February 2026) are cited as opening major export markets, with FTAs with UAE, Australia, Japan, South Korea and UK adding further access.
- [Demand drivers] Automotive expansion (rising polyester content per vehicle for airbags, seatbelts, headliners, carpets and interior upholstery), PLI for polyester fabrics generating derived upstream yarn demand, the post-COVID athleisure boom, and China+1 / Bangladesh-Sri Lanka disruption redirecting global textile sourcing to India.
- [Governance] Board is chaired by Mr. Rajkumar Satyanarayan Agarwal (41+ years in textiles, Managing Director of SVG Fashions since 1984), with Mr. Sandiip Satyanarayan Agarwwal as Whole-Time Director & CFO (31+ years, Director of SVG Fashions since 1994) - i.e. common leadership with the promoter group.
- [Industry sizing] The deck states the polyester yarn market in India is ~Rs 550bn and that PSF + PFY domestic demand is in the range of ~5.0 mn.t annually, with POY/PFY constituting 70-75% of total polyester consumption.
